items.scene:
Narrator: We live in families. People in families help each other. They love each other, too. Not all families are the same. There are many kinds of families. Meet Seb. He's seven years old. Seb's family is big. He lives with his mother, father, three brothers, and two sisters.

Seb's family: We work together.

Narrator: This is Mandy. She's eight years old. She has one brother. They live with their grandmother and grandfather.

Mandy's family: We go places together.

Narrator: This is Kim. She's six years old. Her family is small. She lives with her mother.

Kim's family: We spend time together.

Narrator: Which family is like your family? Friends are also important. Friends have fun together, and they help each other, too. Seb, Mandy, and Kim are good friends. They go to school together. They play together every day.

Friends: We share things.

Narrator: Who are your good friends?
items.spokenScene: What is the main idea?
items.answer: Families can be different and still care for one another.
options: Families can be different and still care for one another.
items.hint: Look for the evidence. Listen again if you need to.
items.why: The opening explains that families love and help each other; the examples show different family sizes.
